notes.front: What is Form 8879, IRS e-file Signature Authorization?
notes.back: The form the taxpayer (and the spouse, on a joint return) signs to authorise the electronic filing of their return.
notes.explanation: It is signed after the return has been reviewed and the taxpayer has been told they are ultimately responsible for what it contains.
notes.example: Like signing a consent slip that lets a courier post a parcel in your name: nothing is sent until the slip is signed.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 291
notes.evidence: After reviewing the return and being advised that they are ultimately responsible for the information on the return, the taxpayer (and spouse if filing jointly) must sign Form 8879 before their return is electronically filed.

notes.front: What is quality review of a tax return at a volunteer site?
notes.back: The process that confirms the tax law was applied correctly and the return is free from error, before it is filed.
notes.explanation: The review measures the return against the intake sheet, the taxpayer interview, the supporting documents and the preparer's notes.
notes.example: Like an editor checking an article against the reporter's notes and sources before it goes to print.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 5: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: The quality review process confirms that tax laws were was correctly applied, and the tax return is free from error based on the Form 13614-C, taxpayer interview, available supporting documents, and tax return preparer notes.

notes.front: In a designated review, who quality reviews the returns?
notes.back: A tax-law certified volunteer whose only job is reviewing returns prepared by the other certified volunteers.
notes.explanation: This is the method the IRS volunteer programme office prefers.
notes.example: Like a proofreader at a newspaper who writes no stories of their own and only checks everyone else's.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-1: Quality Review Methods”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: SPEC prefers the designated quality review method. In this process an IRS-tax law certified volunteer is solely dedicated to reviewing returns prepared by other IRS-tax law certified volunteer preparers.

notes.front: What is peer-to-peer review?
notes.back: A certified volunteer preparer, chosen by the site, quality reviews another preparer's returns.
notes.explanation: A site uses it when it cannot use the preferred designated review method.
notes.example: Like two teachers marking each other's class tests because the school has no separate examiner.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-1: Quality Review Methods”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: In this process an IRS-tax law certified volunteer preparer selected by the site may quality review returns of another preparer when the site is not able to use the preferred Designated Review method.

notes.front: What is self-review, and is it allowed?
notes.back: A volunteer quality reviewing a return they prepared themselves. It is not allowed.
notes.explanation: Every return must be reviewed by a different volunteer from its preparer, who is also certified to the level the return requires.
notes.example: Like marking your own exam paper: however careful you are, the mark does not count.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-1: Quality Review Methods”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: Self-Review (volunteer quality reviews a return they prepared) is NOT allowed. All returns must be quality reviewed by a different volunteer than the preparer who is also certified to the level required for the tax return.

notes.front: What is the Quality Review Checklist?
notes.back: The list in Publication 4012 (Tab K) of items a quality reviewer must address on every return.
notes.explanation: The reviewer works through every item while looking at Form 13614-C, the supporting documents, the preparer's comments and the finished return.
notes.example: Like a pilot's pre-flight checklist: each line is checked, none skipped, before take-off.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Every item on the Quality Review Checklist must be addressed while reviewing Form 13614-C, Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, all supporting documents, return preparer comments, and the completed tax return.

notes.front: In e-filing, what is a reject?
notes.back: The IRS turning down an electronically transmitted return, for a specific reason.
notes.explanation: The IRS acknowledges every transmission, and each return in it comes back either accepted or rejected.
notes.example: Like a letter returned by the post office stamped with the reason it could not be delivered.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: The IRS electronically acknowledges the receipt of all transmissions. Returns in each transmission are either accepted or rejected for specific reasons.

notes.front: Which returns prepared at a volunteer site must be quality reviewed?
notes.back: All of them: every return prepared.
notes.explanation: Quality Site Requirement #2 requires every site to use a complete quality review process for all returns, to ensure accuracy.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Quality Site Requirement #2: Intake/Interview and Quality Review Process, requires every site to use a complete quality review process for all returns prepared to ensure accuracy.

notes.front: The quality reviewer must be certified in tax law {{c1::equal to or above}} the level needed to prepare the return.
notes.back: equal to or above
notes.explanation: So a return that needs Advanced certification to prepare also needs a reviewer certified at Advanced or higher.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 5: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: The quality reviewer must be certified in tax law equal to or above the level needed to prepare the tax return.

notes.front: A site prepares returns above the Basic level. What must its quality reviewers do?
notes.back: Certify to the level needed to review those returns.
notes.explanation: Designated and peer-to-peer reviewers may only review returns whose tax issues fall within their own certification level.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-1: Quality Review Methods”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: Designated and peer-to-peer quality reviewers must only quality review returns with tax issues that fall within their certification levels. If the site is preparing tax returns above the Basic certification level, the quality reviewers must certify to the level needed to quality review these returns.

notes.front: What three skills should a quality reviewer have?
notes.back: In-depth knowledge of tax law, the preparation process and the software; effective communication; tact in explaining errors.
notes.explanation: Communication means being able to explain tax law and how it applies to the taxpayer; tact applies to both taxpayers and volunteers.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-1: Quality Review Methods”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: In-depth knowledge of tax law, the return preparation process and tax preparation software.

notes.front: During quality review, the reviewer must confirm the taxpayer's (and a joint-filing spouse's) identity and {{c1::taxpayer identification numbers}}.
notes.back: taxpayer identification numbers
notes.explanation: This is the first component of a thorough quality review in Publication 5838.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-2: Thorough Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: The quality reviewer must confirm taxpayer’s (and spouse’s, if married filing joint) identity and taxpayer identification numbers during the quality review process.

notes.front: During quality review, whose photo identification does the reviewer verify again?
notes.back: The taxpayer's, and the spouse's if they are married filing jointly.
notes.explanation: It is the first item on the Quality Review Checklist: identity was checked at intake and is checked once more at review.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: During quality review process, taxpayer's (and spouse's, if married filing jointly) photo ID is verified again by quality reviewer.

notes.front: Why does the quality reviewer engage the taxpayer in the review?
notes.back: To confirm the taxpayer understands and agrees with the facts on the return.
notes.explanation: The reviewer also explains that incorrect information may delay the processing of the return.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-2: Thorough Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: Engage the taxpayer’s participation in the quality review to confirm their understanding and agreement to the facts of the return. Explain that incorrect information may delay the processing of their return.

notes.front: What must a thorough review confirm about Form 13614-C itself?
notes.back: The return was prepared from an accurately completed form, errors on it were corrected, and the preparer's notes were read.
notes.explanation: The notes and comments section is where the preparer leaves remarks for the reviewer.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-2: Thorough Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: Verify return was prepared using an accurately completed Form 13614-C, Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet. Verify errors identified on Form 13614-C were corrected. Review notes/comments section for any comments left by the preparer.

notes.front: Besides Form 13614-C, what does a thorough review check the return's entries against?
notes.back: All supporting documentation and other information the taxpayer provided.
notes.explanation: Each entry on the return should trace back to something the taxpayer supplied.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-2: Thorough Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: Review all supporting documentation, and other information provided by the taxpayer to confirm entries are correct on the return.

notes.front: Which references does a thorough review use to verify tax law determinations?
notes.back: Publication 4012, Publication 17 and Volunteer Tax Alerts.
notes.explanation: The reviewer checks the preparer's tax law decisions against the same published references, not memory.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-2: Thorough Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: Review tax law references (Publication 4012 and Publication 17, Your Federal Income Tax (For Individuals), and Volunteer Tax Alerts), to verify the accuracy of tax law determinations.

notes.front: What does the checklist ask the reviewer to verify about the two volunteers and the return's scope?
notes.back: The preparer and the reviewer are certified to prepare and review this return, and the return is within scope.
notes.explanation: A return outside the programme's scope, or above either volunteer's level, cannot pass review.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Verify volunteer return preparer and quality reviewer are certified to prepare/review this return and return is within scope of the program.

notes.front: By the end of review, what three things must have happened to errors or incomplete answers on Form 13614-C?
notes.back: Discussed with the taxpayer, corrected, and notated on Form 13614-C.
notes.explanation: The checklist also requires all applicable questions on pages 1 to 3 to have been answered.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Verify all applicable questions on Form 13614-C, Pages 1 through 3 were answered. Any errors or incomplete information were: ◦ discussed with the taxpayer ◦ corrected ◦ notated on Form 13614-C

notes.front: Which part of Form 13614-C must the checklist confirm the volunteer has completed?
notes.back: The grey-shaded area headed 'to be completed by certified volunteer'.
notes.explanation: The area's own heading says who fills it in: a certified volunteer.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: All applicable information in the "to be completed by certified volunteer" gray-shaded area of Form 13614-C is completed

notes.front: Which identifying details must the checklist confirm are correct on the return?
notes.back: Names, addresses, Social Security numbers, ITINs and employer identification numbers.
notes.explanation: Each identifier on the return is compared with the taxpayer's cards and documents.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Names, addresses, SSNs, ITINs, and EINs are verified and correct on the return

notes.front: If the taxpayer can be claimed as someone else's dependent, what does the checklist ask the reviewer to verify?
notes.back: That it is properly recorded in the basic information section of the return.
notes.explanation: It sits with the checklist item on dependency determinations; filing status is a separate item.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Dependency determinations are correct. If Taxpayer can be claimed as a dependent on someone else’s return, verify that it is properly recorded in the basic information section

notes.front: Must the reviewer verify income listed on Form 13614-C when the taxpayer brought no source document for it?
notes.back: Yes. All income on pages 2 and 3, with or without source documents, is verified.
notes.explanation: The checklist item covers income the taxpayer reported orally as well as income backed by forms.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: All Income on Form 13614-C (with or without source documents) indicated on Pages 2 and 3 is verified and correct

notes.front: Which two kinds of tax payment does the checklist require to be correct?
notes.back: Federal income tax withholding and estimated tax payments.
notes.explanation: They form one checklist item, after the credits and Affordable Care Act items and before the banking details.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Federal income tax withholding and estimated tax payments are correct

notes.front: Which banking details does the checklist ask the reviewer to check?
notes.back: The direct deposit or debit details: routing and account numbers, and checking or savings.
notes.explanation: The item covers direct deposit of a refund and direct debit of a payment alike.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Direct deposit/debit and checking/saving routing and account numbers are correct

notes.front: Which two items near the end of the checklist concern how the return is filed and which site filed it?
notes.back: Federal and state return types are correct (e-file or paper), and the site identification number is included and correct.
notes.explanation: The final checklist item is advising the taxpayer of their responsibility after the review.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: Confirm federal and state return types are correct (for example, e-file or paper). • SIDN is included and correct on the return

notes.front: When must taxpayers be told they are responsible for the information on their return?
notes.back: After the quality review, and before they sign the return.
notes.explanation: The advice closes the review: the taxpayer hears it once the return is final, and before committing to it.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-2: Thorough Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: Advise taxpayers before they sign the return of their responsibility for information on their return. This must be done after the quality review process.

notes.front: In what form must the taxpayer be advised of their responsibility for the return?
notes.back: Verbally.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 requires a spoken explanation, given before signing.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-5: Taxpayer Signature Requirement”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: Taxpayers must be advised verbally of their responsibility for the accuracy of the information they provided to complete their tax return before signing.

notes.front: By signing Form 8879 or the return, what does the taxpayer acknowledge?
notes.back: Under penalty of perjury, that the return is true, correct and complete.
notes.explanation: The volunteer tells the taxpayer this as part of the signature requirement.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-5: Taxpayer Signature Requirement”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: Also advise the the taxpayer that by signing either the Form 8879 or the tax return they are acknowledging under penalty of perjury that the return is true, correct and complete.

notes.front: What two conditions must be met before a site may transmit a return?
notes.back: The quality review is complete, and the taxpayer has signed Form 8879.
notes.explanation: Publication 5101 sets out both conditions in its summary of the rules for sites.
notes.source: Publication 5101 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training, “Summary”, PDF p. 62
notes.evidence: Sites must not transmit tax returns before a quality review is completed and the taxpayer has signed the Form 8879, IRS e-file Signature Authorization

notes.front: On a joint return, must both spouses come to the site, and must they come together?
notes.back: Both must come, to prove identity, verify their numbers and sign, but not necessarily at the same time or on the same day.
notes.explanation: Publication 5838 allows the two visits to be separate.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-5: Taxpayer Signature Requirement”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: Taxpayers filing a joint tax return must both be present at the site to validate proof of their identity and verify their TIN and then sign their tax return. They do not have to be at the site at the same time or on the same day, to do this.

notes.front: On a joint return, until when may the return not be e-filed or a copy handed over?
notes.back: Until both spouses' signatures are on Form 8879 (or on the return itself, if filed on paper).
notes.explanation: One spouse's signature is not enough to release the return or a copy of it.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-5: Taxpayer Signature Requirement”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: However, the tax return must not be e-filed, nor a copy provided to the taxpayer(s) until both signatures are secured on Form 8879, IRS e-file Signature Authorization or the tax return when paper filing.

notes.front: What five-digit PIN may a taxpayer use to sign electronically?
notes.back: Any five numbers except all zeros; on a joint return, the spouse needs one too.
notes.explanation: The rule comes from the taxpayer PIN guidelines in Publication 4012's e-file section.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 292
notes.evidence: The PIN can be any five numbers except all zeros. If filing a joint return, a PIN is needed for the taxpayer and spouse.

notes.front: Before the taxpayer signs Form 8879, what are the taxpayers' PINs set to by default?
notes.back: A 1 followed by the last four digits of the Social Security number.
notes.explanation: The default sits in the electronic return record until the taxpayer signs Form 8879.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 291
notes.evidence: The taxpayers’ PINs are defaulted to 1+ the last four digits of the SSN in the electronic return record before the taxpayers sign Form 8879

notes.front: Is a return valid if it is not signed, and who signs a joint return?
notes.back: No, an unsigned return is not valid; both spouses sign a joint return.
notes.explanation: The return should also be dated and the occupation lines completed.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Return Signature”, PDF p. 304
notes.evidence: A return isn’t considered valid unless it is signed. Both spouses must sign if the return is filed jointly.

notes.front: A taxpayer's agent signs under a paper power of attorney. How does the power of attorney reach the IRS?
notes.back: A copy goes with Form 8453 for the site to send once the return is accepted, or it is scanned and attached to the e-file.
notes.explanation: The same process applies even when the power of attorney is not on Form 2848.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Return Signature”, PDF p. 304
notes.evidence: Attach a copy of the taxpayer’s original paper POA to a copy of Form 8453 for the site to send to the IRS once the return is accepted.

notes.front: No executor has been appointed for a taxpayer who died. Who can sign the joint return for them, and how?
notes.back: The surviving spouse, writing 'Filing as surviving spouse' where the return is signed.
notes.explanation: Once an executor or administrator is appointed, the personal representative signs instead.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Deceased Taxpayer”, PDF p. 305
notes.evidence: If no one has yet been appointed as executor or administrator, the surviving spouse can sign the return for the deceased spouse and enter “Filing as surviving spouse” in the area where the return is signed.

notes.front: The quality reviewer finds an error. What must happen next?
notes.back: Discuss it with the original preparer, return the return to them for correction, then quality review it again.
notes.explanation: The second review confirms that every error was dealt with.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-4: Concluding the Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: the quality reviewer must discuss the errors with the original preparer, return the tax return to the original preparer for correction, and then complete a quality review again to ensure all errors were addressed.

notes.front: Errors found in quality review must be corrected and noted on {{c1::Form 13614-C}}.
notes.back: Form 13614-C
notes.explanation: Correcting the return is not enough on its own; the correction is also recorded on the intake sheet.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-4: Concluding the Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: Errors must be corrected and noted on Form 13614-C.

notes.front: When is a quality review complete?
notes.back: When all errors are corrected, Form 13614-C is complete, and the return agrees with the form and the taxpayer's documents.
notes.explanation: Corrections must follow the tax law correctly applied, not just make the numbers match.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-4: Concluding the Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: Quality review is complete when all errors have been corrected on the tax return based on tax law being applied correctly, Form 13614-C complete, and tax return agrees with Form 13614-C and the taxpayer’s supporting documentation.

notes.front: Which comparison does Publication 5838 suggest as a best practice for reviewers?
notes.back: Comparing the current-year return with the prior year's return, if available.
notes.explanation: It helps catch items that belong on this year's return but for which the taxpayer brought no documents.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-4: Concluding the Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: A suggested best practice is for the quality reviewer to conduct a comparison of the current year tax return to the prior year’s tax return, if available. This helps to ensure that nothing is overlooked or omitted that should have been included on the current year tax return but the taxpayer did not bring documentation with them.

notes.front: What must the reviewer ask the taxpayer before printing the return and before signing?
notes.back: Whether the taxpayer has any questions.
notes.explanation: It is the final step of concluding the quality review, before the signature requirement.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-4: Concluding the Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: Finally, the quality reviewer must ask if the taxpayer(s) has any questions prior to printing the return and before the taxpayer(s) signs the return.

notes.front: What, at a minimum, must sites give taxpayers for their records?
notes.back: The Taxpayer Copy print set.
notes.explanation: Relevant worksheets are built into that print set.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-4: Concluding the Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: Sites must provide at a minimum the Taxpayer Copy print set to taxpayers for their records.

notes.front: Which TaxSlayer print set is recommended for conducting a quality review?
notes.back: The Quality Review print set.
notes.explanation: It holds the return plus the worksheets used to prepare it, and highlights totals from key lines.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 5: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: SPEC recommends using the TaxSlayer Quality Review print set to conduct a quality review.

notes.front: Alongside interaction with the taxpayer, what three things must the quality review process cover?
notes.back: Form 13614-C, the source documents and the tax return.
notes.explanation: The review works across all three, with the taxpayer taking part.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Addendum: Quality Review Best Practice”, PDF p. 18
notes.evidence: The quality review process must include interaction with the taxpayer, a review of Form 13614-C and the source documents as well as the tax return as seen in the diagram below.

image.alt: Diagram: three boxes labelled Form 13614-C, Source documents and Tax return, each with an arrow into a central box labelled Quality review; a fourth box, The taxpayer, is joined to the quality review by a two-way arrow marked interaction.
image.credit: Adapted for this deck from IRS Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), Addendum: Quality Review Best Practice, p. 18; the taxpayer box follows the sentence above the diagram

notes.front: Every question checked on pages 2 and 3 of Form 13614-C must have what on the return?
notes.back: A matching entry, or a preparer comment explaining why it is not on the return.
notes.explanation: The comparison is made once Form 13614-C is complete.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Addendum: Quality Review Best Practice”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: Every question checked on pages 2 and 3 must have a corresponding entry on the tax return, or there should be a preparer comment to explain why it is not included on the return.

notes.front: What must happen to a question on Form 13614-C that the taxpayer left unanswered?
notes.back: It is discussed with the taxpayer and marked No, N/A, with a check mark or another marking if it does not apply.
notes.explanation: The reviewer needs a completed Form 13614-C before starting; unanswered questions slow the review because they must be asked again.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Addendum: Quality Review Best Practice”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: Any items not answered must to discussed with the taxpayer and marked with “No”, “N/A”, a check mark, or other markings if it does not apply to taxpayer.

notes.front: Which kind of other income was named among the top five quality errors in the IRS's fiscal year 2025 reviews?
notes.back: Taxable scholarship income.
notes.explanation: The other four were taxpayer addresses, dividend income, retirement income and filing status.
notes.source: Publication 5101 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training, “Fiscal year 2025 top quality errors”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Reporting other income specifically taxable scholarship income

notes.front: Can a return be e-filed while TaxSlayer still shows e-file errors?
notes.back: No. Every e-file error must be corrected first.
notes.explanation: Warnings are handled differently from errors.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 289
notes.evidence: You cannot e-file the return until you correct all e-file errors.

notes.front: A return is filed after the due date with a direct debit. What date must the debit carry?
notes.back: The date the return is transmitted, or a date within the five days before it.
notes.explanation: Before the due date, the debit can be set for the due date or earlier.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 295
notes.evidence: If filing return after the due date, direct debit date must be the same date as the date the return is being transmitted or be within the previous five days of that date.

notes.front: Does e-filing an amended return, or paying manually online, cancel a scheduled direct debit?
notes.back: No, it is not automatically cancelled.
notes.explanation: Taxpayers are told to confirm the debit is withdrawn and that they remain responsible for paying by the due date if it is not.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 295
notes.evidence: A scheduled direct debit will not automatically get canceled if an amended return is e-filed or if the taxpayer makes a manual payment at irs.gov/payments.

notes.front: What must happen to each consent in TaxSlayer before the return can be marked ready for review?
notes.back: It must be accepted, with a date, or declined.
notes.explanation: The consents section lists all consents assigned to the site, in the order they were assigned or created.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 296
notes.evidence: All consents must be accepted (with date entered) or declined (date unnecessary) in TaxSlayer before the return can be marked as ready for review or complete.

notes.front: After preparing a return in TaxSlayer, the preparer selects 'Mark tax return {{c1::ready for review}}'.
notes.back: ready for review
notes.explanation: Once the reviewer confirms the return is accurate, it is marked Approved.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 298
notes.evidence: After you're finished preparing the return, select Mark tax return ready for review. Once the Quality Reviewer confirms the accuracy of the return, mark the return Approved.

notes.front: When may a return be marked 'complete' in TaxSlayer to enable e-filing?
notes.back: Only after it is reviewed with the taxpayer (and spouse, if joint) and they have signed Form 8879 and any state form.
notes.explanation: Marking it complete makes the return available for transmission to the TaxSlayer Processing Center.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 298
notes.evidence: Select Mark tax return as complete to enable e-filing only after it is reviewed with the taxpayer (and spouse if filing jointly) and they've signed Form 8879 and any applicable state form.

notes.front: What is Form 8453 used for?
notes.back: To send the IRS paper supporting documents that cannot be e-filed, such as a power of attorney or Form 8332.
notes.explanation: Form 8949 can also go this way if the taxpayer elects not to report transactions electronically.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Form 8453”, PDF p. 300
notes.evidence: Form 8453 will be used to transmit specific supporting documents that can’t be e-filed.

notes.front: Who transmits the e-file returns from a volunteer site?
notes.back: The site coordinator or a designee.
notes.explanation: The same person receives the acknowledgement or reject for each return.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 334
notes.evidence: The Site Coordinator or designee transmits all the e-file returns.

notes.front: How often must the site review the e-file acknowledgement report?
notes.back: Every day, to see the status of the previous day's returns.
notes.explanation: Each return in a transmission is either accepted or rejected, so the daily report shows which need action.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: The acknowledgement report must be reviewed each day to determine the status of the previous days submitted returns.

notes.front: What is the most common problem behind a rejected e-file?
notes.back: A name or Social Security number that does not match IRS records.
notes.explanation: The site coordinator or designee then contacts the taxpayer, if necessary, to resolve it.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 334
notes.evidence: The most common problem is a name or Social Security number that does not match IRS records.

notes.front: The IRS rejects a return and the site coordinator cannot fix the reason. Within how long must the taxpayer be told?
notes.back: Within 24 hours; the coordinator must take reasonable steps to inform them.
notes.explanation: The taxpayer may need to act, for example by filing on paper.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: the site coordinator must take reasonable steps to inform the taxpayer of the rejection within 24 hours.

notes.front: If the IRS cannot accept the return electronically, what must the taxpayer do?
notes.back: File a paper tax return.
notes.explanation: Paper is the fallback when the electronic route is closed.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: If the IRS cannot electronically accept the return for processing the taxpayer must file a paper tax return.

notes.front: When correcting a rejected return, by how much may total income or AGI change without new signatures?
notes.back: By no more than $50.
notes.explanation: Beyond that, new signatures or authorisations are needed before retransmitting.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: Rejected electronic individual income tax return data can be corrected and retransmitted without new signatures or authorizations if changes don’t differ from the amount on the original electronic return by more than $50 to “Total income” or “AGI,”

notes.front: When correcting a rejected return, by how much may total tax, withholding, refund or amount owed change without new signatures?
notes.back: By no more than $14.
notes.explanation: The site coordinator must give the taxpayer copies of the new electronic return data.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: or more than $14 to “Total tax,” “Federal income tax withheld,” “Refund” or “Amount you owe.” The site coordinator must give taxpayers copies of the new electronic return data.

notes.front: How is the taxpayer's copy of the return assembled?
notes.back: Form 1040 on top, then each form, schedule and attachment in the order of the sequence number in its upper right corner.
notes.explanation: Before handing it over, the volunteer shows the taxpayer the printed copy and checks the key details once more.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 332
notes.evidence: Start with Form 1040 on top o Place each form, schedule, and attachment in the proper sequence, based on the sequence number shown in the upper right corner of the form

notes.front: For how long should taxpayers be advised to keep a copy of their return and tax documents?
notes.back: At least three years.
notes.explanation: The list includes Form 1040 with all attachments, Forms W-2 and 1099, and any Form 8332 or power of attorney.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 333
notes.evidence: Advise taxpayers to keep a copy of the following documents for at least three years:

notes.front: For an e-filed return, which extra document must the taxpayer keep?
notes.back: A copy of the signed Form 8879.
notes.explanation: The site itself is no longer required by the IRS to keep signed copies.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 333
notes.evidence: For e-file returns, taxpayers must also keep a copy of the signed Form 8879, IRS e-file Signature Authorization.

notes.front: Name two things a volunteer does before seeing taxpayers off?
notes.back: Ask whether they have any questions before they leave; explain how to check a refund at 'Where's My Refund?'.
notes.explanation: Among others, the volunteer also gives payment options for a balance due and reminds taxpayers to take their records.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 333
notes.evidence: Ask taxpayers, “Do you have any questions before you leave?” • If the taxpayer is expecting a refund, provide instructions about how to check on the refund status at IRS.gov “Where’s my Refund?”

notes.front: Priya prepared a return, and the site's only designated reviewer is busy. Priya suggests reviewing it herself to save time. What is the right course?
notes.back: B: another certified volunteer, at the return's level, must review it.
notes.choices:
A) Priya reviews it, because she knows the return best
B) Another certified volunteer at the return's level reviews it
C) The taxpayer reviews it and signs
notes.choicesExplained: A is self-review, which is never allowed. C is wrong because the taxpayer takes part in the review but cannot replace the certified reviewer.
notes.explanation: A different volunteer from the preparer must review every return, and they must be certified to the level the return requires.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-1: Quality Review Methods”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: All returns must be quality reviewed by a different volunteer than the preparer who is also certified to the level required for the tax return.

notes.front: A return includes itemised deductions, which need Advanced certification. The free reviewer is certified only at Basic. Can they review it?
notes.back: B: no; the reviewer must hold Advanced certification or higher.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, if the preparer holds Advanced certification
B) No, the reviewer must be certified at Advanced or higher
C) Yes, if the site coordinator agrees
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because each volunteer needs the certification; the preparer's level does not cover the reviewer. C is wrong because a coordinator cannot waive the certification rule.
notes.explanation: A reviewer must be certified at or above the level needed to prepare the return.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 5: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: The quality reviewer must be certified in tax law equal to or above the level needed to prepare the tax return.

notes.front: At a small site, each certified preparer reviews a colleague's returns, because nobody can be spared to review full time. Which method is this?
notes.back: B: peer-to-peer review.
notes.choices:
A) Designated review
B) Peer-to-peer review
C) Self-review
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because designated review needs a volunteer solely dedicated to reviewing. C is wrong because nobody reviews their own return.
notes.explanation: Peer-to-peer review is the fallback when a site cannot use a dedicated reviewer.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-1: Quality Review Methods”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: In this process an IRS-tax law certified volunteer preparer selected by the site may quality review returns of another preparer when the site is not able to use the preferred Designated Review method.

notes.front: The preparer finishes a return after the taxpayer has gone home. The reviewer plans to review it alone and post it for signature. What is wrong?
notes.back: C: the reviewer must contact the taxpayer so they can take part in the review.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing: the taxpayer's part ended at the interview
B) Only that the preparer should review it instead
C) The taxpayer must be contacted to take part in the review
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because the taxpayer takes part in the quality review too. B is wrong because the preparer may never review their own return.
notes.explanation: Taxpayer participation confirms they understand and agree with the facts on the return.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-3: Quality Review Checklist”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: The quality reviewer must contact the taxpayer so that they can participate in the quality review process.

notes.front: While reviewing, Omar sees that a Form 1099-G was never entered on the return. What should Omar do?
notes.back: B: discuss it with the preparer, send the return back for correction, then review it again.
notes.choices:
A) Enter the 1099-G himself and approve the return
B) Discuss it with the preparer, return it for correction, then review it again
C) Note it on Form 13614-C and approve the return
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because corrections go back to the original preparer and the return is then reviewed again. C is wrong because noting an error does not fix it; it must be corrected.
notes.explanation: The review is complete only when every error has been corrected and the return has been reviewed again.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-4: Concluding the Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 16
notes.evidence: the quality reviewer must discuss the errors with the original preparer, return the tax return to the original preparer for correction, and then complete a quality review again to ensure all errors were addressed.

notes.front: A reviewer has just approved a return and the taxpayer is reaching for the pen to sign Form 8879. What must the reviewer do first?
notes.back: A: tell the taxpayer, out loud, that they are responsible for the information on the return.
notes.choices:
A) Tell the taxpayer verbally that they are responsible for the information
B) Nothing: the advice was given at intake
C) Hand over a written notice and let them sign
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because the advice must come after the quality review. C is wrong because the advice must be given verbally.
notes.explanation: The advice comes after the review and before signing, and it must be spoken.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-5: Taxpayer Signature Requirement”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: Taxpayers must be advised verbally of their responsibility for the accuracy of the information they provided to complete their tax return before signing.

notes.front: Ana signs Form 8879 on Monday. Her husband can only come in on Thursday. What should the site do with the joint return?
notes.back: B: hold it until he comes, proves his identity and signs; then it can be e-filed.
notes.choices:
A) E-file it on Monday, as one signature is enough
B) Hold it until he comes in, proves his identity and signs
C) Refuse the return unless both come on the same day
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because a joint return is not e-filed until both signatures are secured. C is wrong because spouses need not come at the same time or on the same day.
notes.explanation: Both spouses must attend and sign, but not necessarily together.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-5: Taxpayer Signature Requirement”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: They do not have to be at the site at the same time or on the same day, to do this.

notes.front: A return has passed quality review, but the taxpayer has left without signing Form 8879. Can the site transmit it now?
notes.back: B: no; the taxpayer must sign Form 8879 first.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, because the quality review is complete
B) No, the taxpayer must sign Form 8879 first
C) Yes, if the preparer signs in the taxpayer's place
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because a completed review is only one of the two conditions. C is wrong because only the taxpayer (and spouse) can authorise the e-file.
notes.explanation: A site may transmit only after both the review and the taxpayer's signature on Form 8879.
notes.source: Publication 5101 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Training, “Summary”, PDF p. 62
notes.evidence: Sites must not transmit tax returns before a quality review is completed and the taxpayer has signed the Form 8879, IRS e-file Signature Authorization

notes.front: A return is rejected overnight because a dependent's name does not match IRS records. The coordinator cannot fix it without the taxpayer. What must the coordinator do?
notes.back: A: take reasonable steps to tell the taxpayer within 24 hours.
notes.choices:
A) Take reasonable steps to tell the taxpayer within 24 hours
B) Wait for the taxpayer to ask about the refund
C) Change the name to match and retransmit without telling anyone
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because the site must inform the taxpayer within 24 hours. C is wrong because the coordinator cannot fix it without the taxpayer, and guessing at identities is not a fix.
notes.explanation: An unfixable reject must be reported to the taxpayer within a day.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: If the IRS rejects the electronic portion of a taxpayer’s individual income tax return for processing and the site coordinator cannot fix the reason for the rejection, the site coordinator must take reasonable steps to inform the taxpayer of the rejection within 24 hours.

notes.front: Fixing a reject changes the refund by $30. Can the site retransmit without new signatures?
notes.back: B: no; a refund change of more than $14 needs new signatures or authorisations.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, because the change is under $50
B) No, because the refund changed by more than $14
C) Yes, because rejected returns never need new signatures
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because the $50 limit applies to total income and AGI, not the refund. C is wrong because the no-new-signature rule has limits.
notes.explanation: The refund, total tax, withholding and amount owed have a tighter tolerance than total income and AGI.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: or more than $14 to “Total tax,” “Federal income tax withheld,” “Refund” or “Amount you owe.”

notes.front: The taxpayer says she earned $600 cash for occasional tutoring but has no form for it. The intake sheet lists it. What does the quality review do with it?
notes.back: C: verify it is correctly on the return, even without a source document.
notes.choices:
A) Ignore it, since there is no form
B) Remove it from Form 13614-C
C) Verify it is correctly on the return even without a document
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are wrong because the checklist covers all income on Form 13614-C, with or without source documents.
notes.explanation: Income reported on the intake sheet is verified whether or not a form supports it.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: All Income on Form 13614-C (with or without source documents) indicated on Pages 2 and 3 is verified and correct

notes.front: Form 13614-C has 'Unemployment benefits' checked, but the return shows no unemployment compensation and there is no preparer comment. What should the reviewer conclude?
notes.back: A: something is wrong; a checked item needs a matching entry or a comment explaining its absence.
notes.choices:
A) There is a problem to resolve before the return can pass
B) Nothing, because entries can be left off if small
C) Nothing, because the software checks this automatically
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are wrong: every checked question on pages 2 and 3 must have a corresponding entry on the return or a preparer comment.
notes.explanation: The reviewer resolves the gap with the preparer and taxpayer before approving the return.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Addendum: Quality Review Best Practice”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: Every question checked on pages 2 and 3 must have a corresponding entry on the tax return, or there should be a preparer comment to explain why it is not included on the return.

notes.front: The greeter checked the couple's photo identification at intake. At review, the reviewer wants to skip that step. Is that right?
notes.back: B: no; the reviewer verifies both spouses' photo identification again.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, identity is only checked once
B) No, the reviewer verifies photo identification again
C) Yes, if the couple are known to the greeter
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because the checklist requires the reviewer to verify photo identification again. C is wrong because the checklist item applies at every review.
notes.explanation: Verifying identity again is the first item on the Quality Review Checklist.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: During quality review process, taxpayer's (and spouse's, if married filing jointly) photo ID is verified again by quality reviewer.

notes.front: A return has been marked ready for review and Approved. The taxpayer has not yet signed Form 8879. Can the preparer mark it complete?
notes.back: B: no; it is marked complete only after the taxpayer signs Form 8879.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, Approved is enough
B) No, the taxpayer must sign Form 8879 first
C) Yes, if the state return has no form to sign
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because Approved confirms accuracy, not authorisation. C is wrong because Form 8879 is required whatever the state return needs.
notes.explanation: Marking the return complete enables e-filing, so the signature must come first.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 298
notes.evidence: Select Mark tax return as complete to enable e-filing only after it is reviewed with the taxpayer (and spouse if filing jointly) and they've signed Form 8879 and any applicable state form.

notes.front: TaxSlayer shows no e-file errors but two warnings. Can the return be e-filed?
notes.back: A: yes, after reviewing each warning to make sure the return is accurate.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, after each warning has been reviewed
B) No, all warnings must disappear first
C) Yes, and warnings can be ignored
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because only errors block e-filing. C is wrong because each warning must still be reviewed.
notes.explanation: Warnings, unlike errors, do not stop e-filing, but they are not to be ignored.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 289
notes.evidence: You can still e-file the return with warnings, but review each warning to ensure that you completed the return accurately.

notes.front: A taxpayer asks whether she can throw away this year's tax papers once the refund arrives. What is the advice?
notes.back: C: keep the return and documents for at least three years.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, once the refund arrives
B) Keep them until the end of this year
C) Keep them for at least three years
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are wrong because taxpayers are advised to keep a copy of the return and tax documents for at least three years.
notes.explanation: Taxpayers must keep records that prove their income and expenses.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 333
notes.evidence: Advise taxpayers to keep a copy of the following documents for at least three years:

notes.front: It is a busy Saturday. The coordinator suggests skipping quality review for simple wage-only returns. Is that allowed?
notes.back: B: no; every return prepared must be quality reviewed.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, for returns with only Form W-2 income
B) No, every return must be quality reviewed
C) Yes, if the preparer is certified at Advanced
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong because Quality Site Requirement #2 requires a complete quality review process for all returns prepared, whatever their size or the preparer's level.
notes.explanation: The requirement exists to ensure accuracy, and it makes no exception for easy cases.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Quality Site Requirement #2: Intake/Interview and Quality Review Process, requires every site to use a complete quality review process for all returns prepared to ensure accuracy.

notes.front: A reviewer is unsure whether the preparer applied the dependency rules correctly. What should the reviewer check the determination against?
notes.back: C: the tax law references, such as Publication 4012, Publication 17 and Volunteer Tax Alerts.
notes.choices:
A) Their own memory of last season's rules
B) What the taxpayer believes the rule is
C) Publication 4012, Publication 17 and Volunteer Tax Alerts
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are wrong because a thorough review verifies tax law determinations against the published references.
notes.explanation: Reviewing the references is one of the components of a thorough quality review.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “5-2: Thorough Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: Review tax law references (Publication 4012 and Publication 17, Your Federal Income Tax (For Individuals), and Volunteer Tax Alerts), to verify the accuracy of tax law determinations.

notes.front: A couple filing jointly on paper leave with their return, but only one spouse has signed it. Is the return valid as it stands?
notes.back: B: no; a joint return needs both spouses' signatures.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, one signature is enough on paper
B) No, both spouses must sign a joint return
C) Yes, if it is dated
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong because a return is not valid unless it is signed, and both spouses must sign a joint return.
notes.explanation: The signature makes the return valid; a date alone does not.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Return Signature”, PDF p. 304
notes.evidence: A return isn’t considered valid unless it is signed. Both spouses must sign if the return is filed jointly.

notes.front: A reviewer opens the Taxpayer Copy print set to review a return. Which print set is recommended for the review instead?
notes.back: A: the Quality Review print set.
notes.choices:
A) The Quality Review print set
B) The Taxpayer Copy print set is the right one
C) No print set; review on the data-entry screens only
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because the Taxpayer Copy is what the taxpayer keeps. C is wrong because the Quality Review print set is the recommended tool for review.
notes.explanation: The Quality Review print set holds the forms, schedules and worksheets needed to verify the entries.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 5: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 14
notes.evidence: SPEC recommends using the TaxSlayer Quality Review print set to conduct a quality review.

notes.front: A site coordinator plans to check e-file acknowledgements every Friday. Does that meet the requirement?
notes.back: B: no; the acknowledgement report must be reviewed every day.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, weekly is enough
B) No, it must be reviewed every day
C) Yes, if no rejects are expected
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong because the report must be reviewed each day to find the status of the previous day's returns.
notes.explanation: The report shows which of the previous day's returns were accepted and which were rejected.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: The acknowledgement report must be reviewed each day to determine the status of the previous days submitted returns.

notes.front: A return comes back rejected. Which problem does the training guide name as the most common cause?
notes.back: A: a name or Social Security number that does not match IRS records.
notes.choices:
A) A name or Social Security number that does not match IRS records
B) A missing occupation line
C) A refund over a set amount
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are not causes the training guide names; it names the mismatched name or number as the most common problem.
notes.explanation: A mismatch with IRS records on a name or number is the problem the guide singles out.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 334
notes.evidence: The most common problem is a name or Social Security number that does not match IRS records.

notes.front: How does designated review differ from peer-to-peer review?
notes.back: In designated review the reviewer only reviews; in peer-to-peer review a preparer also reviews colleagues' returns.
notes.explanation: Designated review is preferred; peer-to-peer is used when a site cannot manage it. Either way, nobody reviews their own return.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Quality Review Process”, PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: Designated Review – This preferred quality review method uses a designated quality reviewer. This is a volunteer who is solely dedicated to reviewing returns prepared by the other volunteers at the site.

notes.front: In TaxSlayer's e-file section, how do errors differ from warnings?
notes.back: Errors block e-filing until corrected; warnings do not, but each must be reviewed.
notes.explanation: The software lists both when you open the e-file section.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 289
notes.evidence: You cannot e-file the return until you correct all e-file errors.

notes.front: In correcting rejects, which amounts carry the $50 tolerance and which the $14?
notes.back: $50: total income and AGI. $14: total tax, federal withholding, refund and amount owed.
notes.explanation: Within those limits, a corrected reject can be retransmitted without new signatures.
notes.source: Publication 5838 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Intake/Interview and Quality Review Handbook, “Chapter 6: Duties After Submission of Returns to the IRS”, PDF p. 17
notes.evidence: if changes don’t differ from the amount on the original electronic return by more than $50 to “Total income” or “AGI,” or more than $14 to “Total tax,” “Federal income tax withheld,” “Refund” or “Amount you owe.”

notes.front: In TaxSlayer, what is the difference between marking a return Approved and marking it complete?
notes.back: Approved: the reviewer confirms it is accurate. Complete: after the taxpayer signs Form 8879, it enables e-filing.
notes.explanation: The two steps match the two conditions for transmission: a finished review and a signature.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: TaxSlayer Basic Quality Review Print Set”, PDF p. 303
notes.evidence: Once the Quality Reviewer confirms the accuracy of the return, the return should be marked Approved. When the return is shared with and Form 8879 is signed by the taxpayer(s), select the Mark tax return as complete button on the submission page in TaxSlayer.
